newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BA says Australia flights not hit by strike.
newsitem.headline: BA says Australia flights not hit by strike.

text.p: British Airways (BA) Plc said on Tuesday it planned to operate all of its flights between Australia and London, Singapore and Bangkok as scheduled despite the world-wide strike expected later this week.
"Services between Australia and London, Singapore and Bangkok will not be affected," BA said in a statement released in Australia.
BA said it expected to operate about 55 percent of all its long-haul intercontinental flights out of Heathrow and 35 percent out of Gatwick.

The 72 hour strike is due to start at 0500 GMT on Wednesday (3.00 p.m. Wednesday in Australia) and end at 0500 GMT on Saturday. BA's chief executive Robert Ayling is pushing ahead with a plan to save one billion pounds ($1.7 billion) by the end of the century, but cuts have been opposed by the unions who attack Ayling's aggressive management style.
BA is also in dispute with ground staff over its plans to sell its catering division at London's Heathrow.
BA said it expected to fly extra services above those announced under the contingency plans because more cabin crew than expected had said they would work during the strike.
BA said those booked on non-Australian services affected by the strike would be rebooked onto other BA flights where possible or transferred to other airlines.
BA's partner airlines, including Qantas Airways Ltd, would be favoured when transferring passengers.
BA was unable currently to estimate how much the strike would cost the airline.
BA said it planned to operate about 35 percent of its European flights out of Heathrow, but would operate all its European flights out of Gatwick.
